entries.ar: الصدق والكذب أصلهما في القول، ماضيا كان أو مستقبلا، وعدا كان أو غيره، ولا يكونان بالقصد الأول إلا في القول، ولا يكونان في القول إلا في الخبر دون غيره من أصناف الكلام، ولذلك قال: ومن أصدق من الله قيلا [النساء/ 122] ، ومن أصدق من الله حديثا [النساء/ 87] ، واذكر في الكتاب إسماعيل إنه كان صادق الوعد [مريم/ 54] ، وقد يكونان بالعرض في غيره من أنواع الكلام، كالاستفهام والأمر والدعاء، وذلك نحو قول القائل: أزيد في الدار؟ فإن في ضمنه إخبارا بكونه جاهلا بحال زيد، [وكذا إذا قال: واسني في ضمنه أنه محتاج إلى المواساة، وإذا قال: لا تؤذني ففي ضمنه أنه يؤذيه] . والصدق: مطابقة القول الضمير والمخبر عنه معا، ومتى انخرم شرط من ذلك لم يكن صدقا تاما، بل إما أن لا يوصف بالصدق، وإما أن يوصف تارة بالصدق، وتارة بالكذب على نظرين مختلفين، كقول كافر إذا قال من غير اعتقاد: محمد رسول الله، فإن هذا يصح أن يقال: صدق، لكون المخبر عنه كذلك، ويصح أن يقال: كذب، لمخالفة قوله ضميره، وبالوجه الثاني إكذاب الله تعالى المنافقين حيث قالوا: نشهد إنك لرسول الله ... الآية [المنافقون/ 1] ،
entries.en: **Al-ṣidq** (truthfulness) and **al-kadhib** (falsehood) have their origin in speech — whether of the past or of the future, whether a promise or something else. By primary intent they belong only to speech, and within speech only to the declarative statement (*al-ḳabar*), not to the other classes of utterance. Hence He said: **{And who is more truthful than God in speech?}** [al-Nisā' 4:122]; **{And who is more truthful than God in discourse?}** [al-Nisā' 4:87]; **{And mention in the Book Ishmael; indeed he was true to his promise}** [Maryam 19:54]. They may, however, occur incidentally (*bi-l-ʿaraḍ*) in other kinds of utterance — the interrogative, the imperative, the supplication. So when someone says, “Is Zayd in the house?”, contained within it is a statement that the speaker is ignorant of Zayd's condition. [Likewise if he says, “Assist me,” contained within it is that he stands in need of assistance; and if he says, “Do not harm me,” contained within it is that the other is harming him.] Truthfulness is the correspondence of the utterance with the speaker's inner conviction and with the thing reported, both together. Whenever one of these conditions is broken it is not complete truthfulness; rather, either it is not described as truthful at all, or else it is described as truthful in one respect and false in another. Take an unbeliever who says, without believing it, “Muḥammad is the Messenger of God.” It is sound to say he spoke truly, since the matter reported is indeed so; and sound to say he lied, since his utterance contradicts his inner conviction. It is in this second respect that God, exalted be He, pronounced the hypocrites liars when they said: **{We bear witness that you are indeed the Messenger of God}** … the verse [al-Munāfiqūn 63:1].
entries.note: The bracketed clause (“Likewise if he says…harming him”) is supplied by the editor from the manuscript tradition and is bracketed in the printed text. The Kīlānī / Dār al-Maʿrifa edition prints it unbracketed and reads لا تؤذ for لا تؤذني, and reads مما where this edition reads معا (“both together”).

entries.ar: والصديق: من كثر منه الصدق، وقيل: بل يقال لمن لا يكذب قط، وقيل: بل لمن لا يتأتى منه الكذب لتعوده الصدق، وقيل: بل لمن صدق بقوله واعتقاده وحقق صدقه بفعله، قال: واذكر في الكتاب إبراهيم إنه كان صديقا نبيا [مريم/ 41] ، وقال: واذكر في الكتاب إدريس إنه كان صديقا نبيا [مريم/ 56] ، وقال: وأمه صديقة [المائدة/ 75] ، وقال: فأولئك مع الذين أنعم الله عليهم من النبيين والصديقين والشهداء [النساء/ 69] ، فالصديقون هم قوم دوين الأنبياء في الفضيلة على ما بينت في «الذريعة إلى مكارم الشريعة» .
entries.en: **Al-ṣiddīq** is one from whom truthfulness issues abundantly. It is said: rather, the word is applied to one who never lies at all. It is said: rather, to one from whom lying is not even possible, through his habituation to truthfulness. It is said: rather, to one who is truthful in his word and in his belief, and who realises his truthfulness in his deed. He said: **{And mention in the Book Abraham; indeed he was a man of truth, a prophet}** [Maryam 19:41]; and He said: **{And mention in the Book Idrīs; indeed he was a man of truth, a prophet}** [Maryam 19:56]; and He said: **{And his mother was a woman of truth}** [al-Mā'ida 5:75]; and He said: **{Those are with those whom God has favoured — of the prophets, the truthful, and the witnesses}** [al-Nisā' 4:69]. The *ṣiddīqūn*, then, are a people ranking just below the prophets in excellence, as I have set out in *al-Dharīʿa ilā Makārim al-Sharīʿa*.
entries.note: The Kīlānī / Dār al-Maʿrifa edition omits the citation of Idrīs (Q. 19:56) entirely, passing straight from Abraham to Mary's mother — almost certainly an eye-skip, the two verses being near-identical in wording.

entries.ar: وقد يستعمل الصدق والكذب في كل ما يحق ويحصل في الاعتقاد، نحو: صدق ظني وكذب، ويستعملان في أفعال الجوارح، فيقال: صدق في القتال: إذا وفى حقه، وفعل ما يجب وكما يجب، وكذب في القتال: إذا كان بخلاف ذلك.
entries.en: *Ṣidq* and *kadhib* are also used of whatever proves true and comes to be settled in belief, as in “my supposition proved true,” or “proved false.” They are used, too, of the acts of the limbs: one says he was true in battle, meaning he discharged its due and did what must be done and as it must be done; and he was false in battle, when it was otherwise.

entries.ar: قال: رجال صدقوا ما عاهدوا الله عليه [الأحزاب/ 23] ، أي: حققوا العهد بما أظهروه من أفعالهم، وقوله: ليسئل الصادقين عن صدقهم [الأحزاب/ 8] ، أي: يسأل من صدق بلسانه عن صدق فعله تنبيها أنه لا يكفي الاعتراف بالحق دون تحريه بالفعل، وقوله تعالى: لقد صدق الله رسوله الرؤيا بالحق [الفتح/ 27] ، فهذا صدق بالفعل وهو التحقق، أي: حقق رؤيته، وعلى ذلك قوله: والذي جاء بالصدق وصدق به [الزمر/ 33] ، أي: حقق ما أورده قولا بما تحراه فعلا،
entries.en: He said: **{Men who were true to the covenant they made with God}** [al-Aḥzāb 33:23] — that is, they realised the covenant by what they made manifest in their deeds. And His words **{That He may question the truthful about their truthfulness}** [al-Aḥzāb 33:8] — that is, He questions the one truthful with his tongue about the truthfulness of his deed, alerting us that acknowledging the truth does not suffice without pursuing it in action. And His words, exalted be He, **{God has certainly fulfilled His Messenger's vision in truth}** [al-Fatḥ 48:27] — this is truthfulness by deed, namely realisation; that is, He made his vision come true. Of the same kind are His words **{And he who brought the truth and confirmed it}** [al-Zumar 39:33] — that is, he realised in deed what he had put forward in word.

entries.ar: ويعبر عن كل فعل فاضل ظاهرا وباطنا بالصدق، فيضاف إليه ذلك الفعل الذي يوصف به نحو قوله: في مقعد صدق عند مليك مقتدر [القمر/ 55] ، وعلى هذا: أن لهم قدم صدق عند ربهم [يونس/ 2] ، وقوله: أدخلني مدخل صدق وأخرجني مخرج صدق [الإسراء/ 80] ، واجعل لي لسان صدق في الآخرين [الشعراء/ 84] ، فإن ذلك سؤال أن يجعله الله تعالى صالحا، بحيث إذا أثنى عليه من بعده لم يكن ذلك الثناء كذبا بل يكون كما قال الشاعر: إذا نحن أثنينا عليك بصالح ... فأنت الذي نثني وفوق الذي نثني
entries.en: Every excellent act, outward and inward alike, is expressed by *ṣidq*, and the act so described is annexed to it, as in His words **{In a seat of truth with a Sovereign Omnipotent}** [al-Qamar 54:55]; and likewise **{That they have a sure footing with their Lord}** [Yūnus 10:2]; and His words **{Cause me to enter by an entrance of truth and bring me out by an exit of truth}** [al-Isrā' 17:80]; **{And grant me a tongue of truth among those who come after}** [al-Shuʿarā' 26:84]. For that is a petition that God, exalted be He, make him righteous, such that if one who comes after him praises him, that praise would be no lie, but would be as the poet said: *When we praise you for some good / you are the very thing we praise, and beyond what we praise.*
entries.note: A single line of ṭawīl; the hemistich division is marked … in the printed text and is given here with a solidus.

entries.ar: وصدق قد يتعدى إلى مفعولين نحو: ولقد صدقكم الله وعده [آل عمران/ 152] ، وصدقت فلانا: نسبته إلى الصدق، وأصدقته: وجدته صادقا، وقيل: هما واحد، ويقالان فيهما جميعا. قال: ولما جاءهم رسول من عند الله مصدق لما معهم [البقرة/ 101] ، وقفينا على آثارهم بعيسى ابن مريم مصدقا لما بين يديه [المائدة/ 46] ،
entries.en: **Ṣaddaqa** may govern two objects, as in **{God had certainly fulfilled to you His promise}** [Āl ʿImrān 3:152]. *Ṣaddaqtu fulānan* — I ascribed truthfulness to him; *aṣdaqtuhu* — I found him truthful. It is said the two are one, and are used in both senses alike. He said: **{And when a messenger came to them from God, confirming what was with them}** [al-Baqara 2:101]; **{And We caused Jesus son of Mary to follow in their footsteps, confirming what was before him}** [al-Mā'ida 5:46].

entries.ar: ويستعمل التصديق في كل ما فيه تحقيق، يقال: صدقني فعله وكتابه.
entries.en: **Al-taṣdīq** is used of everything in which there is verification: one says, “his deed confirmed me,” and “his writing confirmed me.”

entries.ar: قال تعالى: ولما جاءهم كتاب من عند الله مصدق لما معهم [البقرة/ 89] ، نزل عليك الكتاب بالحق مصدقا لما بين يديه [آل عمران/ 3] ، وهذا كتاب مصدق لسانا عربيا [الأحقاف/ 12] ، أي: مصدق ما تقدم، وقوله: «لسانا» منتصب على الحال، وفي المثل: صدقني سن بكره .
entries.en: He said, exalted be He: **{And when a Book came to them from God, confirming what was with them}** [al-Baqara 2:89]; **{He has sent down upon you the Book with the truth, confirming what was before it}** [Āl ʿImrān 3:3]; **{And this is a Book confirming, in the Arabic tongue}** [al-Aḥqāf 46:12] — that is, confirming what came before; and His word *lisānan* stands in the accusative as a circumstantial qualifier (*ḥāl*). And in the proverb: *ṣadaqanī sinna bakrihi* — “he told me the truth about the age of his young camel.”

entries.ar: والصداقة: صدق الاعتقاد في المودة، وذلك مختص بالإنسان دون غيره، قال: فما لنا من شافعين ولا صديق حميم [الشعراء/ 100- 101] . وذلك إشارة إلى نحو قوله: الأخلاء يومئذ بعضهم لبعض عدو إلا المتقين [الزخرف/ 67] ،
entries.en: **Al-ṣadāqa** — friendship — is truthfulness of conviction in affection, and this belongs to man and to no other. He said: **{So we have no intercessors, nor any devoted friend}** [al-Shuʿarā' 26:100–101]. That alludes to the like of His words **{Close friends, on that Day, will be enemies to one another — except the God-fearing}** [al-Zuḳruf 43:67].

entries.ar: والصدقة: ما يخرجه الإنسان من ماله على وجه القربة كالزكاة، لكن الصدقة في الأصل تقال للمتطوع به، والزكاة للواجب، وقد يسمى الواجب صدقة إذا تحرى صاحبها الصدق في فعله. قال: خذ من أموالهم صدقة [التوبة/ 103] ، وقال: إنما الصدقات للفقراء [التوبة/ 60] ، يقال: صدق وتصدق قال: فلا صدق ولا صلى [القيامة/ 31] ، إن الله يجزي المتصدقين [يوسف/ 88] ، إن المصدقين والمصدقات [الحديد/ 18] ، في آي كثيرة.
entries.en: **Al-ṣadaqa** is what a person gives out of his wealth by way of drawing near to God, like *al-zakāt*; but *ṣadaqa* is properly said of what is given voluntarily, and *zakāt* of what is obligatory. The obligatory may yet be called *ṣadaqa* when its giver pursues truthfulness in his act. He said: **{Take alms from their wealth}** [al-Tawba 9:103]; and He said: **{Alms are only for the poor}** [al-Tawba 9:60]. One says *ṣaddaqa* and *taṣaddaqa*. He said: **{He neither gave alms nor prayed}** [al-Qiyāma 75:31]; **{Indeed God rewards those who give alms}** [Yūsuf 12:88]; **{Indeed the almsgiving men and the almsgiving women}** [al-Ḥadīd 57:18] — in many verses.

entries.ar: ويقال لما تجافى عنه الإنسان من حقه: تصدق به، نحو قوله: والجروح قصاص فمن تصدق به فهو كفارة له [المائدة/ 45] ، أي: من تجافى عنه، وقوله: وإن كان ذو عسرة فنظرة إلى ميسرة، وأن تصدقوا خير لكم [البقرة/ 280] ، فإنه أجرى ما يسامح به المعسر مجرى الصدقة . وعلى هذا ما ورد عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم «ما تأكله العافية فهو صدقة» ، وعلى هذا قوله تعالى: ودية مسلمة إلى أهله إلا أن يصدقوا [النساء/ 92] ، فسمى إعفاءه صدقة، وقوله: فقدموا بين يدي نجواكم صدقة، [المجادلة/ 12] ، أأشفقتم أن تقدموا بين يدي نجواكم صدقات [المجادلة/ 13] ، فإنهم كانوا قد أمروا بأن يتصدق من يناجي الرسول بصدقة ما غير مقدرة. وقوله: رب لولا أخرتني إلى أجل قريب فأصدق وأكن من الصالحين [المنافقون/ 10] ، فمن الصدق أو من الصدقة.
entries.en: **Taṣaddaqa** — of what a person relinquishes of his own right it is said that he “gave it as alms,” as in His words **{And for wounds, retaliation; but whoever gives it away as charity, it is an expiation for him}** [al-Mā'ida 5:45] — that is, whoever relinquishes it. And His words **{And if the debtor is in hardship, then respite until ease; and that you remit it as charity is better for you}** [al-Baqara 2:280] — for He made what is forgiven the man in hardship run the course of alms. On this basis, too, is what has come down from the Prophet, God bless him and grant him peace: “what the foraging creatures eat of it is alms.” And likewise His words, exalted be He: **{and a blood-payment delivered to his family, unless they remit it as charity}** [al-Nisā' 4:92] — so his waiving of it is named *ṣadaqa*. And His words **{Then offer alms before your private consultation}** [al-Mujādala 58:12]; **{Have you been afraid to offer alms before your private consultation?}** [al-Mujādala 58:13] — for they had been commanded that whoever consults the Messenger privately should give some alms, of no fixed amount. And His words **{My Lord, if only You would grant me respite for a brief term, so that I might give alms and be among the righteous}** [al-Munāfiqūn 63:10] — this is either from *al-ṣidq* or from *al-ṣadaqa*.
entries.note: The Kīlānī / Dār al-Maʿrifa edition misreads فدية (“a ransom”) for ودية (“and a blood-payment”) at Q. 4:92; the reading here is correct.

entries.ar: وصداق المرأة وصداقها وصدقتها: ما تعطى من مهرها، وقد أصدقتها. قال تعالى: وآتوا النساء صدقاتهن نحلة [النساء/ 4] .
entries.en: **Ṣidāq** of a woman — also *ṣadāquhā* and *ṣaduqatuhā* — is what she is given of her dower; and *aṣdaqtuhā* means I assigned her a dower. He said, exalted be He: **{And give women their dowers as a free gift}** [al-Nisā' 4:4].
